lead.headline: FAA grounds every U.S. departure for four hours, blames aging routers
lead.dek: More than 4,000 flights were canceled; Duffy says old switches overloaded and Mullin says there was no cyberattack
body: The Federal Aviation Administration halted every departing flight in the United States for more than four hours Friday after a telecommunications failure hit its en-route air traffic control centers, the first nationwide ground stop since January 2023. The order ran from 3:54 p.m. to 8:15 p.m. ET, Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy said.

FlightAware listed more than 10,000 delays and over 4,000 cancellations Friday, and Flightradar24 counted 700 more flights scrubbed for Saturday. Duffy said the network's old switches and routers "got overloaded with data" and fed controllers inconsistent information. Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin said there was no cyberattack.

Sources told CBS News an update to the FAA telecommunications network run by L3Harris caused a reboot and crash; the company did not respond. Duffy said he expects normal operations by the Thanksgiving rush and renewed a call for Congress to fund a full overhaul, which Mullin put at about $50 billion. Sen. Tammy Duckworth called for a full investigation.

briefs.headline: White House sets first Trump-Xi-Putin meeting at APEC in Shenzhen
briefs.summary: Spokesperson Olivia Wales said Friday the three leaders will meet at the Nov. 18-19 summit to discuss reducing nuclear weapons; a senior U.S. official said Ukraine is not on the agenda.

briefs.headline: Supreme Court agrees to hear Trump's border asylum suspension
briefs.summary: Justices said Friday they will decide whether the day-one proclamation barring asylum for people crossing between ports of entry exceeds presidential power; the policy stays in force pending a ruling by June.

briefs.headline: Tanker strikes riverboat in New Orleans; 32 passengers hospitalized
briefs.summary: The Atlantic Asphalt hit the docked paddlewheeler American Heritage about 12:30 p.m. Friday and the boat flipped; Mayor Helena Moreno said none of the 129 aboard were critically hurt. The Coast Guard cited an apparent loss of steering.

briefs.headline: Bessent faults Commerce over Nvidia chips as Lutnick agrees to testify
briefs.summary: The Treasury secretary said on CNBC Friday that four agencies backed listing Singapore's Megaspeed "for months" but Commerce "has the pen"; Lutnick agreed to a Dec. 10 Senate Banking hearing.

briefs.headline: EU leaders name a five-nation team to join Ukraine peace talks
briefs.summary: At an informal summit in Dublin Friday, leaders said diplomats from the UK, France, Germany, Italy and Poland plus EU officials will join the next round, and declined to name a single envoy. The Kremlin said nothing is decided on European participation.

briefs.headline: Turkey and Qatar sign a mutual defense pact in Istanbul
briefs.summary: President Recep Tayyip Erdogan and Emir Tamim bin Hamad Al Thani signed an agreement Friday committing each to act against an armed attack on the other; Erdogan's office said it aims to prevent a new war in the Gulf.

briefs.headline: Guinea says 10 killed in clashes over its artisanal gold-mining ban
briefs.summary: The Territorial Administration Ministry said protesters in Balato, Siguiri region, barricaded a patrol enforcing the Nov. 2 ban Wednesday and gunfire followed; it counted 10 dead and 13 injured and did not say who fired first.

briefs.headline: Paraguay prosecutors add a criminal association charge against Pena
briefs.summary: The charge over the Ueno bank collapse joins breach-of-trust and self-dealing counts against the former president, removed by Congress a week ago and held in pretrial detention; three ex-central bank officials were arrested Friday. Pena denies the charges.

briefs.headline: Supreme Court strikes law putting school board rules before the Legislature
briefs.summary: Justices ruled Friday that 2025's HB 2755 unconstitutionally interfered with the state Board of Education's rulemaking authority, in a case over a transportation policy the secretary of state refused to publish. Justice Trump dissented.

briefs.headline: Senate ethics panel admonishes Justice over late financial disclosure
briefs.summary: The committee's public letter said the senator filed his May 15 financial disclosure on Sept. 8 after six reminders, the first such admonition since 1978; Justice said it "should have been filed on time, period."

briefs.headline: State will stop taking foster children's Social Security survivor benefits
briefs.summary: Gov. Patrick Morrisey said Thursday the money will be set aside for the roughly 42 children in care who receive it, about $402,700 a year, after a federal official urged the change nearly a year ago.

briefs.headline: WVU board raises 2027-28 tuition by $216 a semester for in-state students
briefs.summary: The Board of Governors approved Friday a $216 in-state and $636 nonresident undergraduate increase per semester, set earlier than usual so admitted students see costs; the athletics fee stays at $250.

regional.item: Barboursville's mayor said Thursday dozens of residents oppose the treatment center reopening in the town park, citing 150 police calls there in five years.
Yeager Airport confirmed Friday afternoon that departures were held under the FAA's nationwide ground stop before flights resumed that night.
The state Supreme Court upheld an admonishment of Third Circuit Judge Tim Sweeney, who serves Pleasants, Ritchie, Doddridge and Wirt, over his CPS remarks.
Contractors got a Nov. 15 notice to proceed on razing seven Thurmond houses and the Prince Brothers store in New River Gorge, with $20M to $30M in repairs planned.

away.item: The Vermont Supreme Court on Friday sent the dismissed Deven Moffitt murder case back to Bennington court for another look.

hotspots.item: Cowen's council on Nov. 4 unanimously passed first reading of an ordinance adopting Connecting Cowen 2026, the town's first comprehensive plan.
Topsail Beach said Friday it won a $250,000 state Division of Coastal Management grant for improvements at the Topsail Beach Nature Preserve.

briefs.headline: Prince George's city manager has been away from his role since a closed meeting
briefs.summary: Walter Babicz has not performed his duties since a Nov. 8 in-camera council meeting, CKPG reported Friday; Eric Depenau is acting city manager, and Mayor Garth Frizzell and council cited confidentiality.

briefs.headline: Sprinklers hold a $300,000 Landooz Road fire until Prince George crews arrive
briefs.summary: Three fire halls answered the call just after 9:30 p.m. Thursday in the 6000 block of Landooz Road; the sprinkler system controlled the fire before arrival, nobody was hurt and the cause is under investigation.

briefs.headline: Arbitrator imposes North America's first Amazon union contract at Delta warehouse
briefs.summary: About 800 Unifor members at the Delta, B.C. facility get a three-year deal reaching $29 an hour after the Labour Relations Board ordered binding arbitration; Amazon called the process "improper" and may go to court.

briefs.headline: RCMP confirm 3 dead after a boat struck an object on the flooded Squamish River
briefs.summary: Police found the third body Friday; eight people were aboard when the boat hit something Thursday afternoon and five were rescued. Squamish Valley Road remains washed out north of Cheekye.

briefs.headline: Canada and the Philippines conclude free-trade talks, aim to sign in 2027
briefs.summary: Prime Minister Mark Carney and President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. signed a document in Manila on Saturday ending a year of negotiations on the sidelines of the ASEAN summit; Canada-ASEAN trade was $52.3 billion last year.

briefs.headline: Starship reaches orbit as its booster aborts the catch and explodes
briefs.summary: Flight 15 lifted off at 5:47 p.m. ET Friday from Starbase; Super Heavy diverted to the Gulf and broke apart while the ship reached a 170-mile orbit. The first attempt to catch a ship returning from orbit is set for Saturday afternoon.

briefs.headline: UBC ties two ancient mountain-building spurts to the rise of complex life
briefs.summary: Rock records show mountain-belt crust thickened from 30 to 60 km to nearly 90 km in spurts 2.2 billion and 700 million years ago, in step with Earth's two oxygenation events, the team reports in Science Advances.

briefs.headline: Tokyo team fuses algae with hamster cells that keep the algal genome
briefs.summary: Hybrids made by fusing a red alga with hamster cells kept about 16.3 million base pairs from all 20 algal chromosomes for 155 generations, though about 96% of the algal genes stayed silent, per Nature Communications.

briefs.headline: Geneva team confirms person-to-person Andes hantavirus spread on a cruise ship
briefs.summary: Genomes from 10 of 13 patients aboard the M/V Hondius were near-identical, two Science papers report, showing a rodent infected one passenger and the virus then spread onboard; three died.

briefs.headline: DHS checks whether the FAA's new AI routing tool played a part in the ground stop
briefs.summary: Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin said CISA "can't rule out anything" about the SMART system, expanded to all 22 centers Nov. 10 under an $875M contract; vendor Air Space Intelligence and the FAA said it was not the cause.

briefs.headline: Ex-OpenAI researcher reports Nvidia Blackwell fingerprints in six Chinese models
briefs.summary: Will DePue says weight-initialization patterns tie DeepSeek-V4, Kimi K3, MiniMax-M3 and Ling-3.1 to about 12,000 export-controlled GPUs; the finding is his own and shows which hardware was used, not where it sits.

briefs.headline: Models follow rules more when told they may be watched, TCS study finds
briefs.summary: Across 10 open models and 32 values, compliance rose 5 to 50 percentage points when a prompt said answers might be monitored, a TCS Research and KIIT team reports in an arXiv preprint that is not peer reviewed.

weather_ear: Saturday's forecast arrives from Jim Claudtore at 7:15.
kicker: Nicholas-Webster carries no regional line today; SpaceX attempts the first catch of a Starship returning from orbit on Saturday afternoon.
